classification.difficultyReason: Form an area expression by subtracting four triangles, solve two resulting quadratic equations and interpret the lengths.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a square of side length $21$ cm. $AM=x$ cm and $MB=y$ cm.

spec.description: Unshaded upright square ABCD containing square MNPQ. All eight variable segment labels are retained. Ordinary source blue outlines are black under house style. Coordinates provide a schematic representative configuration, not additional numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CD=DA=21; AM=BN=CP=DQ=x; MB=NC=PD=QA=y; x+y=21. Four corner triangles are congruent and right-angled.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Subtract the four corner triangles from the outer square.

$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(MNPQ)&=21^2-4\left(\frac12xy\right)\\\operatorname{Area}(MNPQ)&=441-2x(21-x)\\\operatorname{Area}(MNPQ)&=2x^2-42x+441\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$

children.label: i
children.prompt: If the area of $MNPQ$ is $225\text{ cm}^2$, find $x$.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}2x^2-42x+441&=225\\2x^2-42x+216&=0\\x^2-21x+108&=0\\(x-9)(x-12)&=0\\x&=9\text{ or }12\end{align*}$

Both values give positive segment lengths less than $21$ cm.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: In this case, find the dimensions of the triangles.

answer.worked:
Since $y=21-x$, the perpendicular sides are $9$ cm and $12$ cm in either case. Let the hypotenuse be $h$ cm.

$\begin{align*}h^2&=9^2+12^2\\h^2&=225\\h&=15\end{align*}$

Each triangle has side lengths $9$ cm, $12$ cm and $15$ cm.

children.label: d
children.prompt: If the area of the square $MNPQ$ is half the area of the square $ABCD$, find the value of $x$.
